card.longDescription: Sid Haig's role as Captain Spaulding was almost very different. Director Rob Zombie had to rewrite the script due to Haig's health issues before filming.

claim_evidence.beat: Director Rob Zombie originally wrote the script for "3 From Hell" with Captain Spaulding, Otis, and Baby as the three main characters throughout.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: The movie that I prepped to make, and was getting ready to start shooting, it was Captain Spaulding, Otis, and Baby, the three originals.

claim_evidence.beat: Three weeks before filming, actor Sid Haig called Zombie from the hospital, where he was recovering from surgery.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: But three weeks out from shooting, I got a call from Sid Haig. He had been in the hospital, and he had just had surgery, and he was now recovering in a rehabilitation facility.

claim_evidence.beat: Zombie visited Haig and observed he had "changed drastically" and was "tiny as a skeleton" compared to his usual "big and burly" self.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: So, I went to see him, and he had changed drastically from the last time I saw him. Because Sid, he’s big and burly, and now he’s tiny as a skeleton.

claim_evidence.beat: Due to Haig's health, Zombie rewrote the script, creating the character Foxy for Richard Brake to take over many of Spaulding's scenes.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: I created this character Foxy for Richard Brake. [...] A lot of the scenes with Foxy were supposed to be Spaulding and I twisted things around so I didn’t have to rewrite every single thing.

claim_evidence.beat: Lionsgate allowed Zombie to bring Haig in for one day to shoot as much as possible, resulting in Captain Spaulding's brief appearance.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: Lionsgate was fine with me sort of sneaking him in one day to shoot as much as I could. It was on me to make sure that nothing went wrong. So I got him in, I shot everything I could shoot.

claim_evidence.beat: "3 From Hell" was originally planned to feature the three main characters from "The Devil's Rejects".
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: The movie I was getting ready to shoot was the original three — that why it was called 3 From Hell.

claim_evidence.beat: Three weeks before filming, actor Sid Haig, who played Captain Spaulding, fell ill and was deemed unable to make the movie.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: Three weeks out from shooting, the actor Sid Haig, who plays Captain Spaulding, called me. He had been in the hospital and just had an operation and was having some problems, and when I went to visit him, he was in no condition — or I didn’t think he was — to make a movie. But I was hoping, "OK, we’re still three weeks away," which is nothing. He's 80 years old, but maybe he's going to get better, he just had surgery, you know. As another week went by and another week, it became very obvious that his health was not in a place where he was capable of making a movie.

claim_evidence.beat: Out of necessity, director Rob Zombie created the new character Foxy, the half-brother.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: So I, out of necessity for the movie, made up a new character that would be the half-brother.

claim_evidence.beat: Richard Brake was Rob Zombie's first choice for the role.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: The first person I had in mind for that was Richard because I had just worked with him on 31, and I knew he was a great actor and that he would fit in great with these guys, and I thought for sure there’d be chemistry.

claim_evidence.beat: Brake joined the production directly from another film with basically no prep time.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: I called him up, and he was actually in Spain shooting a movie at the time. Luckily, he — I mean, so luckily — he was just wrapping the movie right as we were starting. So he went from that movie right to our movie with basically no prep time whatsoever.

claim_evidence.beat: Bill Moseley and Sid Haig used to joke at conventions that a sequel was impossible because their characters were "dead."
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: For years, Sid Haig and I would be on the horror convention circuit together and we even had a little routine where someone would ask if there would be another Devil’s Rejects , and Sid would call out to me and say “Bill, is there gonna be another Devil’s Rejects ?” and I’d say “Nope,” then he’d say “Why?” we’d count to three and then in unison we’d say “’Cause we’re f****n’ dead!”

claim_evidence.beat: Director Rob Zombie created a new character out of necessity after Sid Haig fell ill and was unable to make the movie.
claim_evidence.supporting_passage: As another week went by and another week, it became very obvious that his health was not in a place where he was capable of making a movie. So then I was left with the fact of, like, what do I do now? We had a script and a movie that we'd spent a year preparing to shoot, and now one of the three main people is unavailable to do it. So I went through a lot of scenarios of maybe just having two people, maybe trying to bring back an old character, but then none of that really was working. So I, out of necessity for the movie, made up a new character that would be the half-brother.

claim_evidence.beat: Sid Haig was only able to be on set for one morning to film his scenes, which were designed to be the least strenuous.

Lionsgate let me bring him in one morning just so I could get something with him. I tried to think of something that was the least strenuous thing I could think of for him to do, so that's why he's sitting in a chair being interviewed.
